items.title: Morning Briefing: Oct. 25, 2026
items.excerpt: Here’s a rundown of all the news you need to start your Sunday, including US President Donald Trump weighing a potential strike on Iran or a deal with Tehran, nearly 1,000 arrests during protests in France, and Houthi claims of missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports and oil facilities. US President Donald Trump said Washington could strike Iran as soon as “tomorrow,” or reach a “big, beautiful” agreement with Tehran, amid reports that he's weighing renewed attacks on the Islamic republic. “We’re thinking about doing it, and maybe tomorrow,” Trump told reporters when asked how far along he was in considering a possible attack. “Do you really think I’m going to tell you if I’m going to do it?” he added. Trump said Iran could still avoid further military action by reaching an agreement with the US, adding that “they want to make a deal, but the problem is, will they hold the deal?” - Nearly 1,000 arrested across France amid protests, figure expected to rise Nearly 1,000 people have been arrested in France during demonstrations over rising costs and poor education standards, and the figure is expected to rise, according to Interior Minister Laurent Nunez. Nunez said the demonstrations had largely proceeded as anticipated, but groups considered at risk of causing trouble had broken away from marches and sought to damage property and attack security forces. “Law enforcement intervened systematically in response to these acts, which were numerous, involving projectile throwing and mortar fire,” he said. He said the number of arrests was significantly higher than the 385 recorded at the same point during last weekend's demonstrations. - Houthis claim to have struck Saudi airports, oil facilities with missiles, drones Yemen's Houthi group claimed that it carried out seven military operations using ballistic missiles and drones against airports, oil facilities, and an air base across Saudi Arabia in retaliation for Saudi airstrikes on Yemen. The group said it had targeted King Khalid International Airport in the capital Riyadh. It also claimed attacks on Saudi oil giant Aramco's facilities in Yanbu and the Rabigh oil refinery, both on the kingdom's western Red Sea coast. Another operation targeted crude oil pumping stations and the East-West oil pipeline, which transports oil from eastern Saudi Arabia to the Red Sea coast, according to a statement. ... - A shooting near a university stadium in the US state of Florida left an unknown number of victims and prompted shelter-in-place alerts, according to authorities and local media. - On the eve of a presidential runoff, Sen. Flavio Bolsonaro leads Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva by a narrow one-point margin, 50.5% to 49.5%, according to a poll. - The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted and destroyed a drone above Saudi Arabia’s capital region of Riyadh. - King Khalid International Airport in the Saudi capital announced that domestic flights and international services operated by national airlines would use designated terminals. - The Israeli army raised its alert to the highest and deployed tens of thousands of troops to several areas in preparation for possible security developments, including missile launches from Iran or Lebanon, three days before the Oct. 27 parliamentary elections, public broadcaster KAN reported. - More than 500 protesters were clashing with police at Porte de Vincennes in eastern Paris as the capital's demonstration came to a close, according to the Paris police prefecture. - Three powerful explosions were heard in Yemen’s interim capital Aden, an Anadolu correspondent reported. - The death toll from an attack on mourners attending a funeral at Hamoud Church in Jordan's southern Karak governorate rose to eight, the health minister said. - A magnitude 6.9 earthquake struck the Pacific Ocean region off Vanuatu, according to the US Geological Survey. - US President Donald Trump said he needs to stop killing Iranian leaders to determine who the US is negotiating with, while reiterating his position that Iran must never be allowed to develop nuclear weapons. - Less than 10 days until the US’ Nov. 3 midterm elections, President Donald Trump voted early in Florida, saying he supported all the Republicans on the ballot before heading to a campaign rally in Georgia. - Israel’s defense minister acknowledged that Israeli forces had forcibly displaced 2,000 Palestinians from their homes in Hebron in the southern occupied West Bank. - Hundreds of homes are without power while transport has been disrupted amid weather warnings in the UK due to Storm Boelo, according to media reports. - Spanish police intervened after protests organized by young people in Barcelona turned violent. - Fighting broke out between protesters and police in several Italian cities, with police officers using tear gas and water cannons in Rome, Turin, and Bologna, the ANSA news agency reported. - Thousands of Israelis demonstrated in Tel Aviv against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, three days before Knesset elections, amid demands to replace his government and hold it accountable for its failures. - The Russian Embassy in Tehran denied reports that Russian experts had left the Bushehr nuclear power plant in southern Iran. - More than 14,000 Ethiopians have fled deadly fighting in southern Ethiopia into neighboring Kenya, humanitarian officials said, noting that more than a dozen people have been killed in clashes between rival communities. - items.excerpt: More than 400,000 protest across France, challenging Macron as Paris clashes erupt PARIS (AP) — Clashes erupted in Paris as a mass march drew to a close Saturday. More than 400,000 people rallied across France over school funding and soaring living costs, challenging President Emmanuel Macron. Police made nearly 1,000 arrests. The Paris march began peacefully but turned violent near its endpoint. Masked protesters hurled objects and fireworks at police, who responded with tear gas and water cannons. The Interior Ministry reported 410,000 protesters nationwide, while the CGT union estimated nearly 800,000. This unrest is testing Macron's authority in the final months of his presidency before elections in May. Ukraine and Russia eye new peace talks — and Melania Trump's mission — but steep obstacles remain KYIV, Ukraine (AP) — Ukraine and Russia have signaled willingness to resume peace talks and back a humanitarian mission led by U.S. First lady Melania Trump, but deep disagreements over territory and security guarantees underscore obstacles to ending the war. U.S. President Donald Trump is pushing for a new round of negotiations, potentially in mid-November, as Russia continues to demand control of Ukrainian regions it illegally annexed but does not fully control. Kyiv rejects any suggestion of unilateral withdrawal and says stronger Western pressure on Moscow is needed to advance peace efforts. Trump casts his midterm ballot early in Florida WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. (AP) — President Donald Trump has cast his ballot in the midterm elections, voting for all Republicans in Florida before speaking at a Georgia rally. Trump and first lady Melania Trump arrived at their West Palm Beach polling location together Saturday after Trump spent the morning at his nearby golf course. Trump has endorsed Republican Rep. Byron Donalds, who is running against David Jolly, a Republican-turned-independent-turned-Democrat, to succeed term-limited Gov. Ron DeSantis. He has also campaigned for Republican Sen. Ashley Moody, who is running to fill the last two years of Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s former Senate term against progressive state lawmaker Angie Nixon.

items.title: Hot PPI and CPI data test Fed patience on rate hikes — NewsNovo
items.excerpt: U.S. inflationary pressures are broadening, testing the Federal Reserve's recent signals of patience on interest rates. Bureau of Labor Statistics data released this week shows price increases accelerating in both wholesale and consumer sectors, complicating the central bank's path ahead. The Producer Price Index rose 1.3% in September, the highest level since 2022 and far above the 0.6% analysts had expected. This followed a strong reading on consumer prices released Wednesday. Additionally, September retail sales increased by 0.8%, double the 0.4% forecast, while the August figure was revised upward. Initial claims for unemployment benefits stood at 199,000, remaining near historic lows. Nationwide financial market economist Oren Klachkin noted that the September PPI report reinforces the message from Wednesday's CPI data that inflation is moving in the wrong direction for the Fed. He added that businesses appear to be passing higher costs onto customers, as the proxy for margins rose significantly in September. Klachkin also pointed to AI-related categories as a source of upside pressure on prices. ... Fed Chair Jerome Powell faces a dilemma as he prepares for a policy meeting concluding on Oct. 28. In a speech at the International Monetary Fund's meetings in Thailand, Powell has a final opportunity to comment before the Fed enters its customary quiet period. Colleagues including New York Fed president John Williams and vice chair Philip Jefferson have signaled in recent weeks that they see little urgency to raise rates at a second consecutive meeting this month. ... If Powell affirms that stance despite the hot price data, it could raise doubts about his determination to bring inflation under control. Conversely, if he appears inclined to raise rates, he risks seeming overly reactive to a couple of economic releases, contrary to his stated goal of making the Fed less dependent on single data points. ... Market reactions have been mixed. Bond yields fell Thursday despite the hot PPI number, reversing a surge seen after Wednesday's CPI release. The policy-sensitive two-year Treasury yield briefly touched 4.95% after Wednesday's CPI data, implying significant Fed rate hikes ahead, before dropping to 4.72% Thursday morning. This move suggests a flight to quality among traders as optimism around the AI buildout fades and semiconductor stocks decline.

items.title: Trump announces Audi will build $4 billion factory in US
items.excerpt: After Donald Trump made the announcement at an election rally in Georgia, the German carmaker confirmed plans for a factory in the US state, but noted car production would only start early next decade. Trump said the German company would make 200,000 cars a year in the new Georgian plant Image: CFOTO/picture alliance US President Donald Trump on Saturday announced that German car producer, Audi, will build a $4 billion (€3.77 billion) assembly plant in the US state of Georgia. Speaking at a campaign rally in Perry, Georgia, Trump said the plant will produce 200,000 SUVs annually. "Think of that. 200,000 cars a year. That's incredible," Trump said. The US president credited his tariff policies for the company's decision to build the plant in the US. ## Europe tries to sway Trump on vehicle tariffs ... The US leader has pressured foreign and domestic businesses to move production to the United States. His tactics included sweeping tariffs on car imports. Last year, Trump's tariffs cost Audi €1.2-billion-euro ($1.4-billion). The latest announcement comes as Trump tries to make a last ditch effort to boost Republican candidates in the battleground state by following through on his promise of reinvigorate American manufacturing ahead of the midterm elections. The Republicans are bracing for losses in the November 3 vote amid rising prices and the ongoing war in Iran. ## What did Audi say? Audi, which is owned by Volkswagen, said the construction of the manufacturing plant is ‌scheduled ​to begin next year, with car production starting in the early 2030s. ## How will US tariffs hit Germany's car exports and imports? The plant is expected to assemble the Audi Q7, Q8 and Q9 SUVs, a US official told Reuters news agency. The company also said the investment will create approximately 4,500 jobs.

President Donald Trump’s net approval rating improved 3 percentage points over the past week, with 46% approving and 51% disapproving in our latest tracker update. That improvement comes as the federal government’s Oct. 1 shutdown remains our most salient story for the third week in a row. It’s just the latest indication that, as we get into more below, the impasse on Capitol Hill may be full of sound and fury, but signifies nothing for the average voter. 36% ... Shutdown ... Trump is set to host Senate Republicans for lunch at the White House today “to celebrate their unity in the government shutdown fight and for passing nominees,” according to Politico, which noted that the party’s push for a Nov. 21 funding extension may need to change as Washington gets closer to the expiration date. Some conservatives are said to be pushing for a continuing resolution that would run until March or even next October, though the idea irks Senate Appropriations Committee Chair Susan Collins (R-Maine). Perhaps most notably: NOTUS reports that some Republican senators — even Collins herself — are beginning to entertain the idea of employing the nuclear option to pass a continuing resolution with a simple majority. On the Obamacare front, Politico also reports that Republicans are ramping up talks with the White House on what kind of premium tax credit expansion the party could support once the government is reopened. The party is said to be considering a year-end health care policy package with a two-year extension of scaled-back ACA subsidies though it’s uncertain how that would be received in the House. Nominees The New York Times reports that Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-S.D.) is among at least four Republican senators who have come out in opposition to Trump’s nomination of Paul Ingrassia to lead the Office of Special Counsel following a Politico report documenting a series of racist text messages. That’s enough Republicans to kill Ingrassia’s nomination even before his planned testimony to the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee on Thursday. Separately, Axios noted that Trump has paused the nomination of former Florida Deputy Attorney General John Guard to fill an open open judicial seat in the Middle District of Florida over his connection with a criminal probe, and The Wall Street Journal points out a “power struggle” between Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Elon Musk-aligned billionaire Jared Isaacman over the stewardship of NASA. Gerrymandering House Democratic leaders in Washington have devised a new congressional boundary map for Illinois that would target Republican Rep. Darin LaHood, aiming to reduce the state’s GOP-leaning districts to two, Punchbowl News reports on the party’s response to GOP gerrymandering efforts. Legislators will be in a veto session next week, but will have to move fast ahead of Illinois' pending filing deadline or move next year’s primary date. U.S.-China Trump has rolled out a list of topics he expects to discuss when he meets next week with Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in South Korea. He pointed to rare earth minerals, fentanyl, soybeans and Taiwan, “underlining the divisive topics the two sides plan to tackle at the negotiating table as a fragile trade truce nears its expiration,” as Bloomberg News put it. ... The stalemate between Republicans and Democrats on Capitol Hill over how to reopen the federal government is mirrored by how voters are analyzing what’s happening in Washington. The situation is largely unchanged since we checked in on which side voters blame, and neither have the numbers. Our fresh tracking data shows that voters are 10 points more likely to say responsibility for the shutdown lies with Republicans in Congress rather than Democrats (46% to 36%), in line with the 11-point spread we measured last week. Shares of voters who blame the following for the shutdown: ... Republican voters, who began the shutdown blaming Democrats by a 15-point margin, are only 9 points more likely to do so today. They’re also 10 points more likely to blame their own side of the aisle than Democrats are (40% to 30%), compared with a 3-point gap we measured ... While voters are more likely to blame Republicans on Capitol Hill for the shutdown, very little has changed about their popularity, or the popularity of Democrats in Congress. On the political front, our read on the generic congressional ballot went unmoved over the past week, with 46% of voters indicating their support for the hypothetical Democratic candidate and 43% backing the unnamed Republican candidate if the midterm elections were held today. By these metrics, the party out of power is winning the shutdown fight — or at least holding its own — when it comes to public sentiment. But Washington’s standoff, to date, has left many Americans thinking a lot like they did before the shutdown began.

items.title: Charli xcx Joins Martin Scorsese's 'What Happens at Night'
items.excerpt: Charli xcx and Martin Scorsese‘s collaboration is extending beyond the cover for her new album “Music, Fashion, Film.” ... Sources tell Variety that the pop star has a cameo in the Oscar-winning director’s upcoming movie “What Happens at Night” alongside Leonardo DiCaprio and Jennifer Lawrence. Described as a Gothic psychological drama, the Apple and StudioCanal production follows an American married couple who travel to a small European town to adopt a baby — but as they struggle to claim their child, the less they seem to know about themselves. Charli’s part in the film is being kept under wraps. She joins a cast that also includes Mads Mikkelsen, Patricia Clarkson and Jared Harris.

items.excerpt: # HYBE Cine Fest 2026 Cinema Event Going Global With Two Live BTS Broadcasts, Concert Films From Seventeen, Tomorrow X Together & More ... The HYBE Cine Fest is going international this year with a weeklong global event hitting theaters in more than 60 territories from Oct. 24-31. After launching in Latin America in 2024 and expanding to Asia in 2025, this year’s collaboration between Trafalgar Releasing and HYBE will feature six different events, including the first-ever airings of two BTS live broadcasts from South America. The BTS WORLD TOUR ‘ARIRANG’ in Buenos Aires: Live Viewing in cinemas will mark the K-pop supergroup’s first-ever performance in Argentina, with screenings slated for Oct. 24 in the Americas and Oct. 25 in the rest of the world. A second BTS show, ARIRANG in SÃO PAULO: Live Viewing, will mark the grand finale of the boy band’s Latin American tour, with screenings slated for Oct. 30 in the Americas and Oct. 31 in the rest of the world. ... The program will also feature screenings of SEVENTEEN’s WORLD TOUR ‘NEW_’ concert film marking the group’s 10th anniversary, as well as TOMORROW X TOGETHER’s ACT : TOMORROW from that band’s fourth world tour. The programming will including a screening of the Seoul kick-off of ENHYPEN’S BLOOD SAGA WORLD TOUR and a HYBE Cheering Party (in 3D) where fans are encouraged to chant and sing along to 3D-enhanced on-screen lyrics and wave their official light sticks to music videos of their favorite HYBE acts (LE SSERAFIM, &TEAM, BOYNEXTDOOR, TWS, ILLIT, KATSEYE, aoen, CORTIS and SANTOS BRAVOS).
